notes.concept: typeface specimen framed as an 'Official Travel Guide' to Montreal — each specimen section is a city attraction
notes.structure: 20 named chapters in one long scroll (26 viewports): enveloppe (hero) -> story -> ligne-du-temps (timeline 2018-2026) -> caroussel-circulaire -> graisses-scroll (weights) -> coulers-attractions (10 attractions, each set in a different weight) -> letter-weights -> scroll-split-caracters -> ligatures-circles -> weights_charts -> languages (506) -> accents-bandeaux (240px accent rows) -> tickets -> point-circle-and-square -> pamphlet -> alternatives-versions
notes.distinctive: French section ids as wayfinding; footer nav uses letter-spaced labels; attractions double as weight demos (content = specimen)

evidence.method: DOM structure probe of main children + ids

notes.per_char_splitting: 206px per-character spans observed ('Already in Use, Worldwide!') — char-level animation rig
notes.system: the product IS the typography: variable font used live, weight axis demonstrated by content, display vs text contrast is a named section
notes.letter_spacing: section labels use spaced caps (rendered as 'S t o r y' in text)

notes.character: cream paper ground with ink text; dark inversions for emphasis chapters; transit orange as wayfinding accent — matches Montreal metro signage theme

notes.platform: Framer (framerusercontent script, framer-* classes) + Lottie (lottie-web 5.12.2 from cdnjs)
notes.scroll_model: Framer scroll transforms: 692 transformed elements, 120 will-change, 23 CSS animations running at rest
notes.no_gsap_no_webgl: no GSAP/Three/Lenis globals — all motion via Framer runtime + Lottie + CSS

observed: variable font (PP Neue Montreal Text Variable)

inferred.claim: Scroll-driven transforms are Framer's built-in effect system, not custom JS
inferred.basis: framer-* class naming + no animation library globals

inferred.claim: Lottie used for small illustrative animations (dots, ticket graphics)
inferred.basis: lottie_svg script loaded; no canvas elements

notes.risk: 120 will-change layers is heavy; Framer runtime overhead

notes.nav: footer nav with anchor links to all chapters
notes.risk: letter-spaced labels rendered as literal 'S t o r y' text may confuse screen readers; 240px specimen rows are content-free decoration

principles.rule: Concept-first specimen: the product demo is wrapped in a narrative metaphor (travel guide) so every section teaches AND entertains
Content-as-specimen: attractions set in different weights make the weight axis tangible without a chart
One long scroll with named chapters + footer wayfinding = editorial depth without routing complexity
Per-character splitting at display scale turns headlines into motion moments (converges with Phase-1 thoughtful-focus finding)
Palette discipline: cream/ink + one transit accent; inversions mark chapter boundaries

inferences: Framer platform means V0 cannot copy implementation — must independently implement the chapter structure and scroll choreography in vanilla/KINETIC
The 'raw link blue' (#0000EE) reads as an intentional anti-polish gesture matching the guide's utilitarian tone
Variable font live manipulation (weight axis on scroll) is the core specimen mechanic

anti_patterns.issue: 120 will-change elements: layer-promotion excess risks memory pressure on low-end devices
letter-spaced labels as literal spaced text ('S t o r y') harm screen-reader output
